scenes.heading: Finding your first virtual assistant clients

sents.d: Finding your first virtual assistant clients
Small business owners drowning in admin work are often the easiest first clients.

scenes.heading: Busy solo owners need you most

sents.d: Solo entrepreneurs and small business owners who are personally handling admin tasks that don't require their specific expertise are often the most receptive to a VA pitch, since the pain point is immediate and obvious to them.
VA-specific freelance platforms and communities can provide early client volume and reviews, though direct outreach and referrals from your existing network often produce better long-term clients.

Offering a small trial engagement (a defined, limited scope) lets a hesitant first client test the relationship with lower commitment, and can convert into an ongoing retainer once trust is established.

take: Pitch overloaded solo owners and start with a small trial.
